title: Losing Leverage: A Game-Theoretic Simulation of Power After Full Automation
description: Throughout history, rulers have needed large numbers of people to work, to pay taxes, and to enforce orders. That need is what made them bargain with, feed and fear their populations, despite the class contempt on both sides. If intellectual and physical automation can handle all productive and military work, the need dissolves. This paper asks what protects people once it does, using a game-theoretic Monte Carlo simulation of six world blocs from 2026 to 2075. It tracks: AI capability and robot build-out; the loss of the public's economic and military leverage; the erosion of democracy; purges inside ruling groups; and the choices those groups make once their populations are no longer needed. It draws on evidence from history, political science, economics and AI forecasting, and includes four restraints on rulers that survived adversarial review against documented cases. We cross-checked it against a pre-specified elicitation from a judgment model. Like war games and the scenario side of climate research, the model cannot predict when events will happen. It can, however, compare futures and show which assumptions drive them. Code, data and results: https://github.com/autonet-code/leverage-sims
